alt: Packet Post's title screen: Pim the owl at the Netville post office. Deliver every packet. Keep every secret.
Say Got It begins: three packets are on the road to the mill office, and the second one has fallen off the van.
concept: say got it, the first round

alt: Four packets this time: one copy fell off the van and one arrived twice, so the extra copy waits by the road.
Design the rule set: three things go wrong on this road, and four rule cards are there to catch them.
The whole journey of a picture in five rule cards, waiting to be put in the right order.
concept: the whole journey of a picture

alt: The big town map: roadworks all over town, and Pim warns that two roads will close.
The second of four packets is on its way across the diamond map, two hops done and two to go.
A big town map with a hop budget: the birthday plan must cross in thirteen hops or fewer.
concept: a town map with a hop budget

alt: Sealed roads wear padlocks: open roads cost one hop, but a snoopy cat reads every packet on them.
Five packets for the zoo: every road on this map meets at the center office, where many hands can carry them.
concept: every road meets at the center office

alt: A tablet holds messages and pictures. Signing out on a shared computer: does the habit protect it, or is it risky?
If one key opens every door, losing it opens them all: a habit card waits to be sorted, safe or risky.
The home router still has its key on a sticker anyone can read. Build a new passphrase from four word tiles.
concept: build a new key from word tiles

alt: The backup rule in four steps: make a second copy, keep it in another place, check it opens, keep it fresh.
concept: the backup rule in four steps

alt: Share or Shield: your mailbox key. Anyone who has it can read your post and send as you, so it stays private.
concept: share or shield: the mailbox key

alt: A note to send: OAK TREE, readable by anyone. Three scrambled readings wait below; only one uses the shift of 5.
A secret word, DAOWQF, with no shift marked on the card. Only trying the wheel will show what it says.
The two-key lockbox card: anyone can click it shut, but only the owner holds the key that opens it.
Crack it by counting: a scrambled message, the Caesar wheel, and a button that counts how often letters appear.
Hide a heart in the open: a grid of squares where a heart appears when the brightness numbers are typed in.
concept: hide a heart in the pixels

alt: Spot the trick: the lesson card names what trick messages do. They rush you, promise prizes and fish for your key.
A trick card from the Game Shop, a sender nobody knows: free coins today only, tap the button to claim them.
A trick card from someone you do not know: it fishes for the street a player lives on.
concept: a stranger asks for your street

alt: Spot the trick, Pro style: the lesson card names the levers. Rush, prizes, and asking for your mailbox key.
A trick wearing a bank's name: for your safety, it says, confirm your mailbox key and your birthday.
concept: a trick wearing a bank's name

alt: A parcel trick: a delivery you never ordered is waiting, and a small fee must be paid within two hours.
A fan club card that knows too much: your dog's name and your birthday, learned from your public profile.
concept: it knows your dog and your birthday

alt: A fun quiz in costume: which dragon are you? It asks for a first pet, a street and a birth month to play.
A real message for once: your teacher, a sender you know, about the field trip forms. Nothing to tap, no rush.
concept: a real message from your teacher

alt: Would you rather use a nickname nobody can trace to you, or your real first name so friends can find you?
Would you rather use a nickname nobody can trace to you, or your real first name so friends can find you?
Would you rather share one photo with the whole world, or ten photos with just ten friends?
concept: one photo for the world, or ten for friends

alt: Would you rather share one photo with the whole world, or ten photos with just ten friends?
concept: one photo for the world, or ten for friends

alt: Would you rather put class work on a page anyone can comment on, or a page only your class can see?
concept: a page anyone can comment on

alt: Would you rather put class work on a page anyone can comment on, or a page only your class can see?
concept: a page anyone can comment on

alt: Would you rather delete an old post you are embarrassed by, or leave it up and laugh about it?
concept: delete an old post, or leave it

alt: Would you rather delete an old post you are embarrassed by, or leave it up and laugh about it?
concept: delete an old post, or leave it

alt: Would you rather share a drawing so everyone can see it, or show it only to your family?
concept: a drawing for everyone, or family only

alt: Would you rather play a free game that always sees where you are, or pay for one that never knows?
concept: a free game that sees where you are

alt: Would you rather ask a trusted adult before every download, or never download anything at all?
Would you rather use a picture someone else made and credit them, or draw your own from scratch?
concept: credit a picture, or draw your own

alt: Would you rather keep photos only on your own tablet, or keep a copy on a service someone else runs?
concept: photos on your tablet, or a copy elsewhere

alt: Trick Inbox, the Boss Round: a mean game-chat message waits in the inbox, one clue found in green and one still hiding.
Trick Inbox, the Boss Round at Pro: a letter claiming an account will be deleted waits in the inbox, one clue found and one still hiding.
Escape the Post Office: six trick locks guard the sorting room door, one for each Defender stamp, and none is open yet.
